goal: Refactor SubmissionRuntime and InterruptRuntime to use one payload-oriented interrupt enqueue path, one GraphEvent-based batch completion contract, and one explicit root-RHI boundary object that preserves both host-side ordering and GPU wait injection.

rules_used: Filter validation output and focus on errors
how_they_apply_here: Do not keep three old interrupt enqueue entry points and add a wrapper on top. Converge on one interrupt task protocol.
Do not keep both SubmissionBatch.completion and SubmissionBatch.sync_completion. A batch must expose one completion concept.
Do not replace GPU prerequisite transport with a pure GraphEvent abstraction if real queue waits still exist. Preserve the minimal data needed for final queue submit injection.
Do not use try/catch as steady-state ownership control. Invalid internal states should fail fast with assert.
Validate every structural checkpoint with the existing RHI translate test path.

facts: SubmissionBatch currently carries both completion and sync_completion.
Sync() and Flush() block on promise<GraphEventRef> sync_completion.

RunSubmissionThread currently mixes root prerequisite injection, per-submit dependency attachment, queue submit scheduling, present scheduling, interrupt event chaining, semantic tail folding, and batch completion fulfillment in one loop.
root_rhi_prerequisites is currently copied into root submits as Array<WaitEvent> and then injected into recorded_submit.wait_events before queue submission.
interrupt_completion_events currently delay task_completion_event by calling event->WaitUntil(task_completion_event). This dependency direction must be preserved.
Queue completion, copy completion, and present completion each have separate enqueue functions with duplicated outer mechanics.

VulkanInterruptRuntime.h also exposes repeated overload sets for IsTaskReady(...), ProcessTask(...), and UnlockTaskCompletion(...), which spreads one logical task protocol across multiple near-parallel interfaces.
Most real semantic differences live in ready polling and process logic, not in queue push mechanics.

design_constraints.title: Interrupt enqueue must be payload-oriented
design_constraints.detail: InterruptRuntime should expose one task-oriented protocol that accepts a unified InterruptTask description. Queue, copy, present, and frame-end work remain different task kinds, but they should not duplicate queue push, locking, notification, or top-level dispatch interface shape.

design_constraints.title: SubmissionBatch must have one completion contract
design_constraints.detail: A batch may represent submit, drain, sync, or flush, but it must expose exactly one completion object and one fulfillment rule. The caller must not branch between completion and sync_completion.

design_constraints.title: Single batch completion is GraphEvent-based
design_constraints.detail: SubmissionBatch should carry one optional GraphEventRef completion_event. Drain, Sync, and Flush all use the same type. Submit batches may leave it null unless ordered completion is explicitly needed.

design_constraints.title: One logical root boundary must still preserve GPU waits
design_constraints.detail: root_rhi_prerequisites should collapse to one RootRhiBoundary object, but that object must still carry the real WaitEvent payload required when recorded submits are finalized into actual queue submissions.

design_constraints.title: Dependency folding must be explicit and readable
design_constraints.detail: RunSubmissionThread may preserve the current semantics, but it should express them through named helpers instead of ad-hoc loops and duplicated per-queue blocks.

design_constraints.title: Normal error handling should assert invariants
design_constraints.detail: Internal ownership bugs and impossible state combinations should be guarded by assert. LOG_ERROR remains for external runtime failures such as translation errors or Vulkan result failures.

design_constraints.title: Behavior must stay unchanged while structure simplifies
design_constraints.detail: Submission ordering, queue waits, present scheduling, interrupt completion timing, readback-facing completion timing, and Sync or Flush semantics must remain unchanged from the caller's point of view.

interrupt_enqueue_duplication.problem: Three enqueue functions build similar task records with only payload-field differences. This duplicates lock, push, and notify logic.

interrupt_interface_duplication.problem: IsTaskReady(...), ProcessTask(...), and UnlockTaskCompletion(...) are each repeated as task-specific overload sets even though they are all dispatch over one logical interrupt task domain.

run_submission_thread_mixed_concerns.problem: RunSubmissionThread currently mixes validation, dependency injection, queue submission, interrupt event chaining, tail folding, present scheduling, and batch completion signaling in one loop body.

batch_completion_ambiguity.problem: SubmissionBatch currently carries both promise<void> completion and promise<GraphEventRef> sync_completion even though both represent ordered completion for that batch.

root_prerequisite_transport.problem: root_rhi_prerequisites is logically one predecessor boundary, but it is transported as copied WaitEvent arrays and injected into root recorded submits early.

exception_suppression.problem: try/catch around completion fulfillment hides ownership mistakes instead of making completion single-owner and explicit.

target_design.overview: SubmissionRuntime prepares one interrupt payload per scheduled completion, enqueues that payload through one InterruptRuntime API, composes GraphEvent dependencies through small helpers, and represents root-RHI prerequisite transport as one explicit boundary object instead of copied wait arrays.

key_structures.name: InterruptPayload
key_structures.purpose: Unified transport object for interrupt-visible completion data such as queue pointer, completion event, allocator retirement, callbacks, signals, present host fence, and frame-end marker metadata.

key_structures.name: InterruptTask
key_structures.purpose: Tagged wrapper consumed by InterruptRuntime. It separates task kind from shared enqueue mechanics and keeps ready or process branching explicit.

key_structures.name: SubmissionBatch.completion_event
key_structures.purpose: Single caller-created GraphEventRef used for Drain, Sync, and Flush. Submit batches may leave it null.

key_structures.name: RootRhiBoundary
key_structures.purpose: Single logical predecessor boundary containing host-side ordering data plus the concrete GPU wait packet needed when a real queue submit is emitted.

submission_batch_model.design: Replace completion and sync_completion with one optional GraphEventRef completion_event on SubmissionBatch.

batch_kinds.completion_rule: completion_event is normally null. If a future caller needs ordered completion for a pure submit batch, it uses the same field and same semantics.
Drain creates completion_event before enqueue. SubmissionThread unlocks it when the drain batch is reached, after all earlier batches have already been consumed.
Sync creates completion_event before enqueue. SubmissionThread snapshots the current semantic tails, attaches them to completion_event with WaitUntil(...), then unlocks completion_event.
Flush uses the same completion_event mechanism as Sync(Present). Any extra flush-only side effect such as present-context flush happens outside the batch result type.

caller_contract: Sync() returns the caller-created completion_event itself, not a promise-produced wrapper event.
Flush() waits on the caller-created completion_event and then runs present-context flush logic.
Stop() unlocks any still-pending completion_event exactly once.
implementation_notes: This removes std::promise<void> and std::promise<GraphEventRef> from steady-state batch flow.
GraphEventRef is already the language used by interrupt completion chaining and semantic tail folding, so using it as the single batch completion type reduces conversion points.

root_boundary_model.design: Replace raw Array<WaitEvent> root_rhi_prerequisites transport with one RootRhiBoundary object.
semantics: host_event represents the ordered boundary in host-side dependency composition and improves readability when helper functions attach prerequisites.
gpu_waits preserves the actual queue wait packet that must still be injected into recorded_submit.wait_events before queue submission.
The new design is not GraphEvent-only. It intentionally keeps both host and GPU faces of the same boundary because the runtime still needs real WaitEvent data at submit emission time.
translation_rules: Enqueue() snapshots one RootRhiBoundary rather than a bare Array<WaitEvent>.
Root submits no longer receive copied prerequisite arrays as long-lived transport state.
RunSubmissionThread uses an AttachRootBoundary(...) helper for host-side dependency expression and an InjectRootBoundaryGpuWaits(...) helper right before actual queue submit scheduling.
Pending RHI tail storage evolves from Array<WaitEvent> to RootRhiBoundary-compatible state.

interrupt_payload_scope.design: InterruptPayload and InterruptTask unify the top-level transport and dispatch shape. They do not erase the real differences between queue, copy, present, and frame-end processing.
rules: The common enqueue path owns lock, push, and notify.
Top-level readiness, processing, and completion-unlock entry points should dispatch on one task type rather than exposing repeated public or private overload sets per concrete task struct.
Task kind continues to drive polling and process behavior inside that single dispatch path.
Do not force one giant payload with meaningless fields for every task kind. Use a tagged payload or variant with shared outer mechanics.
Preserve the existing direction of interrupt_completion_events to task_completion_event dependencies. Existing events must wait for the new task completion event, not the other way around.
Preserve current semantic tail folding behavior for rhi_tail and present_tail until a later checkpoint intentionally changes that model.
Preserve current translate_result validation and external error logging behavior.

principles: Normal control flow should not use try/catch.
Batch completion must be single-owner by construction.

Use assert for invalid internal states such as malformed batch kind and completion_event combinations, missing payload on a scheduled path, null completion_event where a blocking batch requires one, and double-fulfillment attempts.
Use LOG_ERROR for external or recoverable failures such as translation failure, missing translated packets from upstream invalid input, and Vulkan failures.
assert_examples: assert(batch completion_event is unlocked in exactly one place)

checkpoints.title: Define a single interrupt enqueue model
checkpoints.problem: InterruptRuntime currently exposes separate queue, copy, and present enqueue entry points that duplicate outer mechanics.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: There is one interrupt enqueue API for completion work.
Shared task metadata is represented once in a common payload structure.
Task kind differences remain explicit in ready and process logic.
Header-level task handling APIs are also collapsed to one task-oriented dispatch surface instead of repeated overload sets.
tasks: Introduce InterruptPayload and InterruptTask shape in the design.
Move lock, push, and notify behind one code path.
Collapse IsTaskReady(...), ProcessTask(...), and UnlockTaskCompletion(...) into single task-oriented entry points that switch or visit on InterruptTask kind.
Keep queue, copy, present, and frame-end-specific fields only where they are semantically required.
Do not merge task-specific polling and processing into a fake one-size-fits-all handler.

checkpoints.title: Collapse SubmissionBatch to one GraphEvent completion contract
checkpoints.problem: completion and sync_completion split ordered batch completion into two unrelated fields.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: SubmissionBatch owns exactly one completion representation.
Submit, Drain, Sync, and Flush all use the same GraphEventRef-based completion concept.
Caller-side code does not branch on multiple completion fields.
tasks: Replace completion and sync_completion with one optional GraphEventRef completion_event on SubmissionBatch.
Change Drain(), Sync(), and Flush() to create completion_event before enqueue and wait or return that same event.
Add one FinishBatchCompletion(...) helper that fulfills completion_event according to batch kind.
Assert invalid batch kind and completion_event combinations instead of handling them with try/catch.

checkpoints.title: Introduce RootRhiBoundary and preserve GPU wait translation
checkpoints.problem: root_rhi_prerequisites is one chain-wait concept, but it is transported as copied WaitEvent arrays and early injection hides the actual submit-time translation point.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: The previous-RHI boundary is represented by one RootRhiBoundary object.
Host-side readability improves because root prerequisite attachment becomes explicit helper logic.
GPU wait translation remains semantically identical to the current behavior.
tasks: Define RootRhiBoundary with host_event plus gpu_waits.
Replace SnapshotPendingRHITails() and StorePendingRHITails(...) with RootRhiBoundary-aware storage.
Attach the boundary through named helpers rather than direct array copying on SubmitInfo.
Inject boundary.gpu_waits into recorded_submit.wait_events only at the final queue submit emission point.

checkpoints.title: Decompose RunSubmissionThread into explicit dependency and scheduling helpers
checkpoints.problem: RunSubmissionThread currently contains correct-but-mixed dependency and scheduling logic that is difficult to reason about and easy to regress.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Dependency attachment, queue submit scheduling, interrupt payload construction, and present scheduling are split into named helper steps.
The order of operations remains unchanged.
The dependency graph can be read from helper names instead of re-parsing the entire loop.
tasks: Extract root boundary attachment into a helper.
Extract submission-to-submission dependency attachment into a helper.
Extract per-queue recorded submit scheduling into helpers that return a unified scheduling result.
Extract present-stage scheduling into a helper with explicit preconditions.
Preserve the direction of interrupt_completion_events to task_completion_event dependencies.

checkpoints.title: Remove try/catch from steady-state batch completion flow
checkpoints.problem: Exception swallowing around promise fulfillment hides ownership mistakes and makes completion flow harder to trust.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Normal batch completion signaling has no try/catch suppression.
Completion ownership is single-writer and structurally enforced.
Shutdown path and normal path use the same completion model.
tasks: Remove try/catch from pending batch cleanup in Stop().
Remove try/catch from completion fulfillment in RunSubmissionThread().
Restructure ownership so each completion_event can be fulfilled at most once by design.
Use assert for impossible internal states such as double fulfillment or null completion_event on Drain, Sync, or Flush.

checkpoints.title: Validate the structural refactor with existing RHI translate coverage
checkpoints.problem: This refactor changes core submit, sync, present, and interrupt plumbing and can regress behavior while appearing cleaner.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Existing RHI translate tests still pass.
No new validation errors appear in submit, copy, present, or sync paths.
Behavioral equivalence is preserved while code structure simplifies.
tasks: Run testscripts/test_rhi_translate.ps1 after each critical checkpoint.
Pay special attention to present completion timing, readback-facing interrupt completion timing, and Sync(Present) behavior.
Reject any solution that adds new fallback waits, compatibility layers, or try/catch-based ownership control.

execution_order: CP-01: unify the interrupt enqueue shape around InterruptPayload and InterruptTask.
CP-02: collapse SubmissionBatch to a single GraphEvent completion contract.
CP-03: replace root_rhi_prerequisites array transport with one RootRhiBoundary that still carries gpu_waits.
CP-04: split RunSubmissionThread into named dependency and scheduling helpers.
CP-05: remove try/catch from steady-state completion flow and replace it with assert-backed invariants.
CP-06: validate the structural cleanup with the existing RHI translate test path.

test_script.purpose: Build and run TestRHITranslate.exe to validate submit, present, sync, copy-scope, and interrupt completion behavior after structural runtime changes.
usage_notes: Run after any checkpoint that changes batch completion flow, root boundary transport, interrupt enqueue flow, or present scheduling.
Treat new validation errors as regressions even if the executable exits successfully.
Do not use VulkanDevice::WaitIdle() or other emergency waits to mask structural mistakes.

acceptance_criteria: InterruptRuntime accepts one unified completion payload model instead of duplicated enqueue boilerplate.
InterruptRuntime header and implementation use one task-oriented dispatch surface instead of repeated overload families for readiness, processing, and completion unlock.
SubmissionBatch uses one GraphEvent-based completion concept, not parallel completion and sync_completion fields.
root_rhi_prerequisites is replaced by one RootRhiBoundary mechanism that preserves both host-side ordering and final GPU wait injection.
RunSubmissionThread remains semantically correct but is split into readable dependency and scheduling stages.
Normal control flow does not rely on try/catch and instead asserts internal invariants.

risks.title: Over-merging interrupt payloads can blur task semantics
risks.impact: Queue, copy, present, and frame-end tasks become harder to validate if the payload abstraction erases their real differences.
risks.mitigation: Use a tagged payload or variant that shares outer mechanics while preserving task-specific fields explicitly.

risks.title: Collapsing batch completion incorrectly can break Drain, Sync, or Flush
risks.impact: Drain may stop being a simple ordered barrier, or Sync and Flush may stop returning the right frozen event boundary.
risks.mitigation: Keep batch kind explicit and use one caller-created GraphEventRef completion_event whose fulfillment rule is defined per batch kind.

risks.title: Replacing root prerequisite arrays too early can hide GPU wait translation details
risks.impact: Root submissions may lose required predecessor waits if the logical boundary is not translated back to queue waits at the correct point.
risks.mitigation: Use RootRhiBoundary with both host_event and gpu_waits, and inject gpu_waits only at actual queue submit emission time.

risks.title: Helper extraction can accidentally invert event dependencies
risks.impact: Interrupt completion or readback-facing completion may fire too early.
risks.mitigation: Lock the dependency rule that existing interrupt_completion_events must wait for the new task_completion_event and validate this path with tests.

risks.title: Removing try/catch without fixing ownership can introduce shutdown deadlocks
risks.impact: Pending batches may never complete during shutdown or completion may be unlocked twice.
risks.mitigation: Make completion_event single-owner before deleting exception suppression, and assert on malformed internal ownership.
